picks.headline: Authors Guild publishes survey results about copyright registration failures
picks.excerpt: Authors ruled ineligible for the Anthropic settlement discovered their publishers never registered their titles with the U.S. Copyright Office — an administrative failure that is now costing writers real money.
picks.rationale: 500+ authors, 1,400 books: hard data showing publishers skipped a contractual duty that just cost writers $3,000 a title — directly actionable for any author's next contract.

picks.headline: Authors push back as publishers and agents make claims on Anthropic settlement
picks.excerpt: As payouts from the $1.5 billion Anthropic copyright settlement begin, authors say publishers and agents appear to be claiming more than their contractual share of the roughly $3,000 owed per infringed work.
picks.rationale: New beat beyond the publisher-error story already run: literary agencies are claiming a cut despite holding no rights, plus the Aug 10 2022 reversion cutoff authors need to dispute.

picks.headline: AI Updates, Remembering Dolly Parton, and More News for Library Workers
picks.excerpt: Book Riot's weekly roundup for library workers leads with the latest AI developments hitting libraries — from vendor AI features to policy fights over AI-generated material in collections.
picks.rationale: Freshest item in the pool and the only one reporting the physical-supply side: AI firms buying up secondhand stock, rare books routed to an Amazon training facility.

picks.headline: Audible Ramps Up English Translations of European Audiobooks
picks.excerpt: Audible says it has quadrupled the number of titles translated into English from European languages this year, with European translations up 300% year-over-year — and a spokesperson confirmed every one of them was done by humans, not AI.
picks.rationale: Recovery pass pick: the only fresh, non-duplicate AI-angle books story left in the window. At the exact moment Audible is pushing AI narration and AI translation to publishers, its own fastest-growing translation slate is explicitly all-human — a hard datapoint for the human-vs-machine translation question.
